discrepancies: pandas extension dtype vs Polars native dtype.

target_api: pl.Enum(categories) if categories are fixed; otherwise pl.Categorical
functional_description: Defines categorical dtype with allowed categories and orderedness.
usage_limitations: Use pl.Enum([...]) when the allowed categories are known in advance.
discrepancies: pandas supports ordered=True/False; Polars Enum has fixed category set, while Categorical ordering behavior is not a full pandas ordered categorical clone.

functional_description: Returns categories.
usage_limitations: Works for categorical data; for fixed predefined categories, keep the original Enum category list as config.
discrepancies: pandas stores categories in dtype; Polars can retrieve stored categories from categorical Series/Expr, but category mappings should not be treated exactly like pandas categories.

target_api: No one-to-one equivalent; migration pattern: use + "pl.Enum(categories)" + for fixed semantic order, or sort/map manually
functional_description: Indicates whether categories have an ordered relationship.
usage_limitations: If ordered comparisons matter, preserve category order explicitly with Enum or a rank mapping column.
discrepancies: pandas ordered categorical supports ordered comparisons; Polars requires explicit category/order strategy.

target_api: pl.Series("x", values).cast(pl.Enum(categories)) or pl.Series("x", values, dtype=pl.Categorical)
functional_description: Stores categorical values.
usage_limitations: Prefer Enum if categories are fixed; use Categorical if categories are inferred.
discrepancies: pandas Categorical is a separate array-like object; Polars uses Series dtype.

target_api: No direct one-step equivalent; migration pattern: map integer codes to category strings, then cast to pl.Enum(categories)
functional_description: Creates categorical data from integer codes and category labels.
usage_limitations: Need to handle missing code values, usually -1 in pandas, manually.
discrepancies: pandas can construct categorical from physical codes; Polars category physical codes are implementation details and should not be relied on.

functional_description: Returns categorical dtype.
usage_limitations: Inspect schema in Polars.
discrepancies: pandas returns CategoricalDtype; Polars returns Categorical or Enum.

functional_description: Returns categories.
usage_limitations: Keep category list separately if exact allowed category universe matters.
discrepancies: pandas Categorical stores explicit categories, including possibly unused ones; Polars category retrieval reflects stored categories.

target_api: No direct scalar property; migration pattern: store orderedness as metadata/config and enforce with Enum/rank mapping
functional_description: Returns whether categories are ordered.
usage_limitations: Preserve this manually if ordered comparisons/sorting matter.
discrepancies: pandas has ordered categorical metadata; Polars does not mirror the same property model.

functional_description: Returns integer category codes.
usage_limitations: Treat physical codes as implementation detail; do not rely on stable cross-run/category mapping unless controlled.
discrepancies: pandas codes are exposed as categorical codes; Polars physical representation may not be semantically stable.

target_api: No direct method; migration pattern: cast to + "pl.Enum(ordered_categories)" + or create explicit rank mapping
functional_description: Sets categorical as ordered.
usage_limitations: Use ordered category list as config.
discrepancies: pandas changes ordered metadata; Polars needs explicit ordered representation or rank column.

target_api: No direct method; migration pattern: cast to pl.Categorical or treat as string/categorical without ordered comparisons
functional_description: Sets categorical as unordered.
usage_limitations: Remove ordered comparison logic or use plain categorical/string semantics.
discrepancies: pandas ordered flag does not map one-to-one.

functional_description: Cast one or more columns to a specified dtype.
usage_limitations: Map simple dtype casts directly; pandas allows dict of {col: dtype} while Polars uses with_columns + cast per column.
discrepancies: pandas astype works on the whole DataFrame or per column via dict; Polars requires explicit per-column cast expressions.

target_api: No direct Polars equivalent; Polars infers nullable dtypes by default during read.
functional_description: Convert columns to the best possible nullable dtypes that support pd.NA.
usage_limitations: Do not translate directly; Polars natively uses nullable Arrow-backed types.
discrepancies: pandas requires explicit convert_dtypes to opt into nullable types; Polars uses Arrow-backed nullables by default.

target_api: No direct Polars equivalent; Polars infers types at parse time.
functional_description: Attempt to infer better dtypes for object columns.
usage_limitations: No direct mapping; Polars infers types during data loading.
discrepancies: pandas may keep object dtype until infer_objects is called; Polars infers column types at load time.

functional_description: Make a copy of the DataFrame.
usage_limitations: Use df.clone() in Polars; deep/shallow distinction does not apply since Polars DataFrames are immutable.
discrepancies: pandas copy(deep=True/False) controls deep vs shallow copy; Polars clone() always produces an independent copy because DataFrames are immutable.

functional_description: Convert the DataFrame to a NumPy array.
usage_limitations: Polars to_numpy() may require allow_copy=True for zero-copy conversion; null values must be handled before conversion.
discrepancies: pandas index is excluded automatically; Polars DataFrame has no index so all columns are exported directly.

functional_description: Return the first n rows of the DataFrame.
usage_limitations: Direct mapping; default n=5 is the same in both.
discrepancies: No meaningful difference.

functional_description: Return the last n rows of the DataFrame.
usage_limitations: Direct mapping; default n=5 is the same in both.
discrepancies: No meaningful difference.

functional_description: Access a single value for a row/column label pair.
usage_limitations: Polars has no label-based .at accessor; use df.filter(...).select(...).item() or row/column integer indexing.
discrepancies: pandas .at uses label-based indexing; Polars uses integer-position or filter-based access without a direct equivalent.

functional_description: Access a single value for a row/column pair by integer position.
usage_limitations: Use df.item(row, col) in Polars for integer-position scalar access.
discrepancies: pandas .iat uses row/col integer position; Polars item() does the same but with explicit arguments.

functional_description: Access a group of rows and columns by label(s) or a boolean array.
usage_limitations: Polars has no label-based index; replace df.loc[mask] with df.filter(mask) and df.loc[:, cols] with df.select(cols).
discrepancies: pandas loc relies on the Index; Polars is index-free and uses filter/select/slice for the same operations.

functional_description: Purely integer-location based indexing for selection by position.
usage_limitations: Replace df.iloc[start:end] with df.slice(start, length); replace df.iloc[i] with df.row(i); replace df.iloc[:, j] with df.select(df.columns[j]).
discrepancies: pandas iloc supports full NumPy-style integer indexing; Polars uses separate slice/row/select methods.

functional_description: Insert a column into the DataFrame at a specified location.
usage_limitations: Use df.insert_column(index, series) in Polars; column must be a Polars Series.
discrepancies: pandas insert modifies in place; Polars insert_column returns a new DataFrame.

target_api: polars.DataFrame.get_columns; iterate with for col in df.get_columns()
functional_description: Iterate over (column name, Series) pairs.
usage_limitations: Polars has no .items() method; use df.get_columns() which returns a list of Polars Series.
discrepancies: pandas .items() is a generator of (name, Series) tuples; Polars uses get_columns() returning a list of Series.

functional_description: Return the column labels of the DataFrame.
usage_limitations: Direct mapping to df.columns in Polars, which returns a list of column name strings.
discrepancies: pandas .keys() returns the Index of column labels; Polars .columns returns a plain Python list.

functional_description: Iterate over DataFrame rows as (index, Series) pairs.
usage_limitations: Replace with df.iter_rows(named=True) or df.to_dicts(); Polars has no index so row index is not yielded.
discrepancies: pandas iterrows yields (index, Series); Polars iter_rows yields tuples or named dicts without an index.

functional_description: Iterate over DataFrame rows as namedtuples.
usage_limitations: Use df.iter_rows() for plain tuples or df.iter_rows(named=True) for dict-like access; named tuple class is not replicated.
discrepancies: pandas itertuples yields namedtuples with Index; Polars iter_rows yields plain tuples without index.

target_api: No direct equivalent; use col = df[name]; df = df.drop(name)
functional_description: Return and drop a column from the DataFrame in place.
usage_limitations: Polars DataFrames are immutable; extract column with df[name] then reassign df = df.drop(name).
discrepancies: pandas pop modifies the DataFrame in place and returns the column; Polars requires a separate select and drop.

target_api: polars.DataFrame.filter; or df[row_index] for simple cross-sections
functional_description: Return a cross-section from the Series/DataFrame by key and level.
usage_limitations: Polars has no MultiIndex; replace with filter expressions or integer row access.
discrepancies: pandas xs is designed for MultiIndex label lookup; Polars has no index and uses filter/slice instead.

target_api: polars.DataFrame.select([col]) if col in df.columns else default
functional_description: Get a column by name, returning a default if the column does not exist.
usage_limitations: No direct Polars equivalent; check df.columns first and use df.select or df[col] with manual fallback.
discrepancies: pandas .get() returns None (or default) for missing columns; Polars raises an error on missing columns.

functional_description: Check whether each element in the DataFrame is contained in values.
usage_limitations: Apply is_in per column via expressions; Polars returns a boolean mask expression rather than a boolean DataFrame.
discrepancies: pandas isin returns a boolean DataFrame of the same shape; Polars is_in is an expression applied per column.

functional_description: Replace values where the condition is False.
usage_limitations: Use polars when/then/otherwise expression pattern; the semantics are inverted compared to pandas (pandas keeps True, Polars when matches True).
discrepancies: pandas where keeps values where cond is True and replaces with other where False; Polars uses when/then/otherwise which is more explicit.

functional_description: Replace values where the condition is True.
usage_limitations: Invert the condition and use when/then/otherwise in Polars.
discrepancies: pandas mask replaces values where cond is True; Polars uses when/then/otherwise with inverted logic.

functional_description: Filter rows by evaluating a query expression string.
usage_limitations: Replace string expression with Polars boolean expressions using pl.col(); Polars filter does not accept string queries.
discrepancies: pandas query accepts a string expression evaluated against column names; Polars filter requires explicit expression objects.

functional_description: Set the given value in the column at the specified integer position.
usage_limitations: No direct Polars equivalent; use with_columns to set values by column name derived from position.
discrepancies: pandas isetitem sets by integer column position in-place; Polars uses with_columns for column-level assignment.

functional_description: Sort the DataFrame by one or more column values.
usage_limitations: Map by to the column name(s), ascending to descending=not ascending; na_position maps to nulls_last.
discrepancies: pandas sort_values uses by= and ascending=; Polars sort uses by= and descending=, with nulls_last controlling null position.

target_api: No direct Polars equivalent; Polars has no index. Use polars.DataFrame.sort on a row-number column if needed.
functional_description: Sort the DataFrame by its index labels.
usage_limitations: Polars has no index; if order matters use a row-number column and sort on it.
discrepancies: pandas sort_index sorts by the Index; Polars is index-free so there is no direct equivalent.

target_api: No direct Polars equivalent; Polars has no MultiIndex.
functional_description: Return Series/DataFrame with requested index/column level(s) removed.
usage_limitations: Polars has no MultiIndex; flatten multi-level columns manually with rename or struct operations.
discrepancies: pandas droplevel removes a level from a MultiIndex; Polars has flat column names and no index levels.

functional_description: Reshape DataFrame from long to wide format using column values as new column headers.
usage_limitations: Polars pivot syntax differs: use on= for column, index=, values=, aggregate_function=. No multi-value support like pandas.
discrepancies: pandas pivot uses index/columns/values kwargs; Polars uses on/index/values/aggregate_function and does not support multi-value pivoting in the same way.

functional_description: Create a pivot table with aggregation over duplicate entries.
usage_limitations: Use polars.DataFrame.pivot with aggregate_function; pandas aggfunc strings map to Polars aggregate_function strings.
discrepancies: pandas pivot_table supports multiple aggfuncs, margins, fill_value; Polars pivot supports one aggregate_function and simpler options.

target_api: No direct Polars equivalent; Polars has no MultiIndex.
functional_description: Rearrange index or column levels using input order.
usage_limitations: Polars has no MultiIndex; not applicable in most migration scenarios.
discrepancies: pandas reorder_levels works on MultiIndex; Polars has flat schema with no index.

functional_description: Return the first n rows ordered by the specified columns in descending order.
usage_limitations: Use df.top_k(n, by=col); Polars top_k is faster than sort().head() for large datasets.
discrepancies: pandas nlargest uses n and columns kwargs; Polars top_k uses n and by kwargs.

functional_description: Return the first n rows ordered by the specified columns in ascending order.
usage_limitations: Use df.bottom_k(n, by=col); Polars bottom_k is faster than sort().head() for large datasets.
discrepancies: pandas nsmallest uses n and columns; Polars bottom_k uses n and by.

target_api: No direct Polars equivalent; Polars has no MultiIndex.
functional_description: Swap levels i and j in a MultiIndex.
usage_limitations: Polars has no MultiIndex; not applicable in most migration scenarios.
discrepancies: pandas swaplevel works on MultiIndex levels; Polars has flat column names and no index.

functional_description: Stack the prescribed level(s) from columns to index, reshaping from wide to long.
usage_limitations: Use df.unpivot(on=cols, index=id_cols); Polars unpivot renamed from melt in Polars >= 0.20.
discrepancies: pandas stack creates a MultiIndex Series; Polars unpivot returns a long-format DataFrame without a MultiIndex.
keywords: stack;unpivot;melt;wide to long;reshape;long format;columns to rows

functional_description: Pivot a level of the index labels from rows to columns, reshaping from long to wide.
usage_limitations: Use df.pivot() as the closest equivalent; Polars has no MultiIndex so the mapping requires manual preparation.
discrepancies: pandas unstack operates on the Index level; Polars pivot uses an explicit column as the source for new column names.
keywords: unstack;pivot;long to wide;reshape;wide format;rows to columns

functional_description: Unpivot a DataFrame from wide format to long format.
usage_limitations: Map id_vars to index=, value_vars to on=, var_name to variable_name=, value_name to value_name= in Polars unpivot.
discrepancies: pandas melt is aliased to DataFrame.melt; Polars renamed melt to unpivot in version 0.20. Both achieve the same wide-to-long reshape.

functional_description: Transform each element of a list-like column into a separate row.
usage_limitations: Direct mapping; Polars explode works on List-type columns. Use pl.col(col).cast(pl.List(...)) if needed first.
discrepancies: pandas explode works on any iterable cell; Polars explode requires the column to be of List dtype.

target_api: No direct Polars equivalent; use df.to_series() if DataFrame has one column.
functional_description: Squeeze 1-dimensional axis objects into scalars.
usage_limitations: For single-column DataFrame use df.to_series(); for single-element use df.item().
discrepancies: pandas squeeze auto-detects 1-D shape and returns a Series or scalar; Polars requires explicit to_series() or item().

functional_description: Assign new columns to a DataFrame, returning a new object.
usage_limitations: Replace df.assign(col=expr) with df.with_columns(expr.alias('col')); lambda references to other new columns in the same call are not supported in Polars.
discrepancies: pandas assign supports lambda referencing other kwargs in the same call; Polars with_columns evaluates all expressions independently.

target_api: No direct Polars equivalent; compute element-wise difference manually.
functional_description: Compare two DataFrames and show the differences.
usage_limitations: Use (df1 - df2) or conditional expressions to find differences; no dedicated compare method in Polars.
discrepancies: pandas compare returns a stacked diff DataFrame; Polars has no equivalent but frame_equal and element-wise ops can serve similar purposes.

functional_description: Join columns of another DataFrame on index or on a key column.
usage_limitations: Polars join requires explicit on= or left_on=/right_on= columns; index-based join (pandas default) has no equivalent since Polars has no index.
discrepancies: pandas join defaults to joining on index; Polars join always requires explicit key columns.

functional_description: Merge DataFrames with a database-style join.
usage_limitations: Map on/left_on/right_on directly; how maps to how in Polars; suffixes maps to suffix= (single tuple in Polars); validate and indicator are not supported.
discrepancies: pandas merge supports indicator column and validate mode; Polars join does not. Polars suffix is a single string, not a two-element tuple.

target_api: No direct Polars equivalent; use polars.DataFrame.join + with_columns to overwrite values.
functional_description: Modify DataFrame in place using non-NA values from another DataFrame.
usage_limitations: Polars DataFrames are immutable; reconstruct by joining and using coalesce or when/then/otherwise.
discrepancies: pandas update modifies in place; Polars requires building a new DataFrame via join and conditional expressions.

target_api: No direct Polars equivalent; use upsample or join with a date range.
functional_description: Convert time series to specified frequency.
usage_limitations: Polars has upsample for upsampling; downsampling requires resample-style group_by_dynamic.
discrepancies: pandas asfreq reindexes to a fixed frequency; Polars uses group_by_dynamic or upsample for time-based frequency operations.

functional_description: Return last row(s) without any NaNs before a given timestamp.
usage_limitations: Use df.join_asof(other, on=key, strategy='backward') for as-of merge; single-row lookup requires additional filtering.
discrepancies: pandas asof is a row lookup for a single key; Polars join_asof performs an as-of merge between two DataFrames.

functional_description: Shift index by desired number of periods.
usage_limitations: Apply shift per column using with_columns; fill_value maps to fill_value in Polars; freq-based shift is not supported in Polars.
discrepancies: pandas shift supports freq-based time shifting for DatetimeIndex; Polars shift is integer-period only.

target_api: No direct Polars equivalent; use df.filter(polars.col(col).is_not_null()).row(0) pattern.
functional_description: Return index for first non-missing value or None if no value is found.
usage_limitations: Polars has no index; find row position with arg_where or filter.
discrepancies: pandas first_valid_index returns the index label; Polars has no index and requires filter/search manually.

target_api: No direct Polars equivalent; filter non-null and take the last row.
functional_description: Return index for last non-missing value or None if no value is found.
usage_limitations: Polars has no index; filter non-null rows and take the last one.
discrepancies: pandas last_valid_index returns the index label; Polars has no index and requires manual row search.

functional_description: Resample time-series data to a new frequency and apply aggregations.
usage_limitations: Replace df.resample(rule).agg() with df.group_by_dynamic(index_column, every=rule).agg(); time offset strings differ between pandas and Polars.
discrepancies: pandas resample uses offset aliases (e.g. 'M', 'D'); Polars group_by_dynamic uses duration strings (e.g. '1mo', '1d'). pandas resample supports closed/label; Polars has period/offset/closed options.

target_api: No direct Polars equivalent; Polars has no PeriodIndex.
functional_description: Convert DataFrame from DatetimeIndex to PeriodIndex.
usage_limitations: Polars has no Period dtype; use date_trunc or group_by_dynamic for period-like operations.
discrepancies: pandas uses PeriodIndex for fiscal/calendar periods; Polars represents periods via duration arithmetic on Datetime columns.

target_api: No direct Polars equivalent; Polars Datetime columns are already timestamp-based.
functional_description: Cast PeriodIndex to DatetimeIndex of timestamps.
usage_limitations: Polars uses Datetime dtype directly; no Period→Timestamp conversion needed.
discrepancies: pandas to_timestamp converts from PeriodIndex; Polars has no PeriodIndex so this conversion is not applicable.

functional_description: Convert tz-aware DatetimeIndex or columns to a target time zone.
usage_limitations: Apply per column: df.with_columns(pl.col(col).dt.convert_time_zone(tz)).
discrepancies: pandas tz_convert operates on the Index or whole DataFrame; Polars applies per column via expression.

functional_description: Localize a tz-naive DatetimeIndex or column to a target time zone.
usage_limitations: Use df.with_columns(pl.col(col).dt.replace_time_zone(tz)) to localize naive datetime columns.
discrepancies: pandas tz_localize sets the time zone on a naive datetime; Polars replace_time_zone does the same per column.

functional_description: Convert a list of dicts or structured array into a DataFrame.
usage_limitations: Use pl.DataFrame(records) or pl.from_dicts(records) for a list of dicts; structured arrays use pl.from_numpy.
discrepancies: pandas from_records handles both structured arrays and list-of-dicts; Polars uses different constructors for each case.

target_api: No direct Polars equivalent; use polars.DataFrame.write_ipc or write_parquet instead.
functional_description: Write DataFrame to an HDF5 file using HDFStore.
usage_limitations: Do not translate to HDF5; prefer write_parquet or write_ipc for Polars columnar storage.
discrepancies: pandas supports HDF5 via PyTables; Polars has no HDF5 writer and recommends Parquet or IPC/Feather.

functional_description: Convert DataFrame to a NumPy record array.
usage_limitations: Use df.to_numpy() for a regular array or df.iter_rows() for row tuples; Polars has no record-array output.
discrepancies: pandas to_records returns a structured NumPy recarray; Polars has no direct equivalent.

functional_description: Render a DataFrame to a console-friendly tabular string.
usage_limitations: Use str(df) or repr(df) in Polars; many formatting options in pandas have no Polars equivalent.
discrepancies: pandas to_string has extensive column/row formatting options; Polars uses its own fixed string representation.

target_api: No direct Polars equivalent; use tabulate library or df.to_pandas().to_markdown().
functional_description: Print DataFrame in Markdown-friendly format.
usage_limitations: Use the tabulate library with df.to_dicts() or convert to pandas first.
discrepancies: pandas to_markdown uses the tabulate library internally; Polars has no built-in markdown formatter.

target_api: No direct Polars equivalent; convert to pandas first with df.to_pandas().plot() or use a dedicated plotting library.
functional_description: Plot the DataFrame using matplotlib as the default backend.
usage_limitations: Convert to pandas or use a plotting library (e.g. hvplot, plotly, altair) that accepts Polars DataFrames directly.
discrepancies: pandas has a built-in plot accessor backed by matplotlib; Polars has no native plot method.

target_api: No direct Polars equivalent; use df.to_pandas().hist() or a dedicated plotting library.
functional_description: Draw histograms of the DataFrame's columns.
usage_limitations: Convert to pandas or use a plotting library.
discrepancies: pandas has a built-in hist method; Polars has no native histogram plot method.

target_api: No direct Polars equivalent; use df.to_pandas().boxplot() or a dedicated plotting library.
functional_description: Make a box plot from DataFrame columns.
usage_limitations: Convert to pandas or use a plotting library.
discrepancies: pandas has a built-in boxplot method; Polars has no native box plot method.

target_api: No direct Polars equivalent; store metadata externally.
functional_description: Dictionary for storing global metadata for the DataFrame.
usage_limitations: Polars has no attrs dict on DataFrames; store metadata in a separate Python dict.
discrepancies: pandas attrs is a mutable dict persisted with the DataFrame; Polars DataFrames carry no arbitrary metadata.

target_api: No direct Polars equivalent; use df.to_pandas().style for Styler functionality.
functional_description: Return a Styler object for HTML rendering with conditional formatting.
usage_limitations: Convert to pandas to use Styler; or use the Great Tables library which supports Polars natively.
discrepancies: pandas style returns a Styler with rich HTML formatting; Polars has no built-in Styler but Great Tables provides equivalent functionality.
